name: Zhang Desheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, Zhejiang Wanma Group (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Wanma Co., SZSE: 002276)
profile: Zhang Desheng founded the Wanma group in Lin'an, Hangzhou, which makes power cables and polymer materials via Zhejiang Wanma (listed 2009) and also controlled Wanma Technology (SZSE: 300698) at its 2017 IPO. Before going into business in 1989 he was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory. Wanma has expanded into EV charging.
interesting_fact: Forbes added him to its billionaire ranks in 2015 on investor hopes for Wanma's electric-vehicle charging business, an energy angle relevant to the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his own business in 1989, Zhang was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory (per Forbes profile).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Some sources say his daughter Zhang Bin chairs the group's tech arm, so check current chair in latest SZSE filings. Best route is via the company's board secretary/IR office. Do not confuse him with the Shaanxi politician of the same name.

name: Ding Shui Po
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Xtep International Holdings (HKEX: 1368)
profile: Ding Shui Po founded Xtep in Fujian in 1999. It began as a manufacturer for international brands before building its own Xtep sportswear brand, and it now also runs Saucony and Merrell in China. He has more than 30 years in the sportswear industry and remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Xtep is a major Chinese running brand. Ding sits on the China Athletic Association's marathon committee (2015) and became a specially invited vice president of the association in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serial executive-education student: Peking U (2004), Tsinghua (2006), CKGSB (2011), CEIBS and Xiamen EMBA (2014), Harvard's Global CEO Program (2018), and CKGSB again in 2023. He was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year China in 2009.
notes: Best route is via Xtep investor relations / corporate communications (Hong Kong). Running/marathon angle could be a hook.

name: Su Ruchun
current_role: Founder and chairman, Huabang Holding Group (华邦控股集团); stepped down as chairman of Huanong Property & Casualty Insurance in April 2025
profile: Su Ruchun (b. 1967) founded Huabang Holding Group, a private conglomerate in real estate, infrastructure and financial-sector investments. It is the largest shareholder (20%) of Huanong P&C Insurance, which he chaired from Sept 2015 until resigning for personal reasons in April 2025.
interesting_fact: He served on the 12th CPPCC National Committee (economic committee) and was vice chairman of the Gansu Federation of Industry and Commerce.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a postgraduate degree and is a nationally registered first-class constructor (一级建造师), a professional engineering qualification that is rare among tycoons.
notes: 2025 Chinese press reports say Huabang Holding is under heavy debt pressure, with share freezes and consumption restrictions on Su. Approach with care, as he is unlikely to be receptive now. No published contacts found. Not related to Huabang Health (002004.SZ).

name: Wong Shou-Yeh
current_role: Chairman, Dah Sing Financial Holdings and Dah Sing Banking Group (Hong Kong)
profile: David Shou-Yeh Wong (b. c.1941, Ningbo) leads Hong Kong's Dah Sing banking group, founded in 1947 with his father Wong Shih-sing as an early chairman. He took the helm in the 1980s and built it into one of Hong Kong's last independent family-controlled banks, with life insurance and mainland bank stakes.
interesting_fact: Dah Sing is often called one of Hong Kong's last independent local banking groups. Wong has chaired it for about four decades.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Ningbo-born member of the Ningbo merchant diaspora in Hong Kong, an alumnus of Diocesan Boys' School, and a former vice-president of the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers.
notes: Sources differ on when he became chairman (1983 or 1987). Very private, so the best route is Dah Sing corporate communications or the company secretary.

name: Liu Jidong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~28.9%), Shenyang Xingqi (Sinqi) Eye Medicine Co. (SZSE: 300573)
profile: Liu Jidong (b. Oct 1957) is a pharmacist and senior engineer. From 1989 to 2000 he ran the Shenyang Xingqi pharmaceutical factory, then founded and has chaired Xingqi Eye Medicine since 2000. Xingqi is now China's leading ophthalmic-drug specialist, driven by its low-dose atropine eye drops for childhood myopia.
interesting_fact: In March 2024 Xingqi's 0.01% atropine sulfate eye drops became the first low-dose atropine product approved in China for slowing childhood myopia, and the shares hit a record high.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in pharmacy and rose through the old Shenyang Xingqi pharmaceutical factory (1989-2000) as technical director, then acting director and director, before founding the company in 2000. He is listed as a 'core technical staff member' in company filings and is a Liaoning Provincial Model Worker.
notes: The board secretary's office (证券部) contact is in Xingqi's annual reports on cninfo.com.cn. Low international media profile.

name: Wang Jianchen
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Shenzhen Edge Medical (精锋医疗, HKEX: 2675)
profile: Dr. Wang Jianchen co-founded Shenzhen Edge Medical in 2017 with Gao Yuanqian to build domestic minimally invasive surgical robots. Edge says it was the first company in China, and the second worldwide, to get approvals for multi-port, single-port and natural-orifice surgical robots. It listed in Hong Kong in January 2026 after raising about HK$1.2bn.
interesting_fact: Edge Medical is a Temasek-backed rival to Intuitive Surgical. Its multi-port robot holds a CE mark, and its Hong Kong IPO in January 2026 drew 15 cornerstone investors.
notes: Some sources say he holds a Tianjin University doctorate (with MIT joint training), but this is unverified. The best route is Edge Medical's IR team, whose contacts are in its HKEX prospectus or annual report. Fortune is shared with co-founder Gao Yuanqian.
